title: Word order, negation and yes/no questions
description: Subject–verb–object, non before the verb, double negatives, and questions by intonation.
objectives: Negate with non and use non … mai / niente / nessuno.
Ask yes/no questions without changing word order.

blocks.text: The neutral order is subject – verb – object, as in English: *La bambina mangia una mela*. Because verb endings show the subject, the subject is often omitted (*Mangia una mela*), and it can move after the verb for emphasis or when it is new information: *Arriva il treno* (Here comes the train).

blocks.title: Adjectives and noun phrases
blocks.text: Inside a noun phrase the order is article – (some adjectives) – noun – (most adjectives): *la piccola casa bianca*.

blocks.title: non goes directly before the verb
blocks.text: Place *non* immediately before the conjugated verb — and before any object or reflexive pronoun attached to it: *Non mangio. Non lo so. Non mi sveglio presto.*

blocks.title: Double negatives are required
blocks.text: With *mai* (never), *niente* (nothing), *nessuno* (nobody) and *più* (no longer), Italian keeps *non* before the verb: *Non piango mai. Non vedo niente. Non c'è nessuno. Non piove più.* If the negative word comes first, *non* is dropped: *Nessuno risponde.*

blocks.title: Intonation, not word order
blocks.text: A statement becomes a question by rising intonation (and a question mark in writing). There is no equivalent of English 'do': *Parli italiano.* (You speak Italian.) → *Parli italiano?* (Do you speak Italian?)
An explicit subject often moves to the end: *È arrivato Marco?* (Has Marco arrived?). Answers: *sì* (yes) — with an accent — and *no*.

examples.en: The little girl eats an apple.

examples.it: La bambina non mangia la mela.
examples.en: The little girl doesn't eat the apple.
There is nobody in the wood.

exercises.prompt: Make the sentence negative and put the words in order: 'The cat does not sleep.'
Order the words: 'I don't wake up early.'
exercises.explanation: non comes before the reflexive pronoun mi.
non … mai: both parts are needed.

mistakes.message: Italian needs non before the verb with mai: Non piango mai.

exercises.explanation: Same word order as the statement, with rising intonation.

exercises.prompt: In *Arriva il treno*, what is *il treno*?
exercises.explanation: The subject can follow the verb, especially with verbs of arriving and appearing. arriva agrees with il treno.

summary: Neutral order: subject – verb – object; subjects are often omitted or placed after the verb.
non goes immediately before the verb and its pronouns.
non … mai / niente / nessuno / più: double negation is normal.
Yes/no questions keep statement order; intonation does the work.

title: Question words and conjunctions
description: chi, che cosa, dove, quando, come, perché, quanto, quale — and joining clauses with e, ma, o, perché, quando, se, mentre.
objectives: Ask open questions with the main question words.
Join two clauses with common conjunctions.

blocks.title: The subject usually follows the verb
blocks.text: In open questions an explicit subject normally comes after the verb: *Dove abita Marco?* *Che cosa fa la mamma?*

blocks.title: quanto agrees, qual è has no apostrophe
blocks.text: *quanto* agrees with its noun: *quanta acqua, quanti anni, quante stelle*. *quale* is truncated before *è* without an apostrophe: *Qual è il tuo nome?*

blocks.caption: Joining clauses
rows: Vuoi il tè o il caffè?

blocks.title: perché = why and because
blocks.text: The same word asks and answers: *Perché piangi? — Perché sono stanco.* Always written with an acute accent: *perché*.

examples.en: I'm staying at home because it is raining.
If it rains, I'll take the umbrella.
The bear is big but gentle.

exercises.explanation: dove → place; quanti → number; chi → person; quando → time; perché → reason.
qual è is written without an apostrophe (quale is truncated, not elided).

exercises.prompt: Complete with ma, perché, se or mentre.
exercises.text: Resto a casa {0} piove. {1} fa bel tempo, andiamo al mare. Il cane è vecchio {2} corre veloce. Il gatto dorme {3} io leggo.
exercises.explanation: reason → perché; condition → se; contrast → ma; simultaneity → mentre.

exercises.prompt: Translate: Where does the fox live?
exercises.explanation: The subject follows the verb in the question.

summary: chi, che cosa, dove, quando, come, perché, quanto, quale.
Explicit subjects usually follow the verb in questions.
e, ma, o, perché, quando, se, mentre, poi join clauses.
perché = why / because; qual è without apostrophe.
